title: Registered load-use replay: detect the hazard at ID into a flop, stall/replay the consumer in EX from MEM, so stall_id is flop-only
motivation:
The champion's recorded critical path (r11s2: from lfsr_20 = imem_data[20] to cpu/u_if/pc_20, modules
u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id -> u_if, 11 cells) is the stall cone: imem_data (flop in the timed wrapper) ->
`head = v0 ? e0 : fresh` -> head_rs1/2 -> hazard_unit load-use compare against ID/EX.rd -> stall_id ->
`accept = imem_ready & ~(v1 & stall_id)` -> accept_f -> pc / ahead_ok / icache CE and the e0/e1 write
enables. stall_id (OR of dmem_stall, load_use, div_stall) fans out to ~260 ID/EX CE pins plus the fetch
queue, and its only late input is the head-field compare. Every cycle-side idea left is capped at a few
percent (predictor work, store buffer ~2%, dmem stalls are i.i.d. and unpredictable), and the last
rounds show that cutting one tail of a shared wall gives about half the predicted gain, but this one cuts
the *front* of the stall cone (head mux + 5-bit compare + `& late_res`) rather than a tail, and the
compare then terminates at a flop D pin (~4 LUT levels) instead of continuing into accept -> pc.
Cycle count is unchanged by construction: the load-use consumer still pays exactly one bubble.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Turn the load-use interlock into a registered "replay" so that stall_id depends on flops only.

Today: at ID, load_use = ID/EX.late_res & (ID/EX.rd == head_rs1 | head_rs2) raises stall_id and flush_id
(bubble into ID/EX) in the same cycle. New scheme (same one bubble, consumer C waits in EX instead of ID):
 1. hazard_unit keeps the ID-time compare (keep the net name `load_use_hazard`, test_pipeline.py probes it)
    but splits it per operand: lu_d1 = ID/EX.late_res & (rd == head_rs1), lu_d2 likewise for rs2. It no longer
    drives stall_id / flush_id. Two new flops lu1_q / lu2_q (clock + reset ports added to hazard_unit):
      consume = if_id_w.valid & ~stall_id          (if_id_w.valid = emit, already redirect-masked)
      if (reset | redirect)  lu*_q <= 0
      else if (dmem_stall)   lu*_q <= lu*_q        (hold: replay waits for the load data to be delivered)
      else                   lu*_q <= consume & lu_d*
    lu_q = lu1_q | lu2_q means "the instruction now in EX consumed, via a stale P1 bypass capture, the
    load/MUL that is now in MEM".
 2. stall_id = dmem_stall | lu_q | div_stall; flush_id = redirect & ~dmem_stall (load-use term removed).
    Every input is a flop (dmem_ready is a flop in the wrapper, ex_mem mem_op / div state / lu_q are flops);
    this is the only thing in front of accept -> pc. Optionally add a decoder-computed `is_div` ctrl bit
    (core_pkg ctrl_t) so div_op in EX needs no 5-bit alu_op compares.
 3. replay_go = lu_q & ~dmem_stall. In that cycle the load/MUL in MEM has mem_res valid. id_stage re-captures
    the stale operand(s) of the held ID/EX instruction from mem_res: rs1_val <= mem_res if lu1_q;
    rs2_val <= mem_res if lu2_q; alu_b <= mem_res if lu2_q & ~ctrl.alu_src; everything else in ID/EX holds.
    Implement it by folding replay into the existing one-hot / priority select terms (p1 leg masked with
    ~replay_go, mem leg selected by lu*_q | (~p1 & p2)) so no extra 2:1 mux level is added behind the
    late mem_res data leg; selects are all early (flop-derived replay terms OR'd into the existing head-compare
    selects), the data legs are unchanged. CE of those three fields = ~stall_id | replay_go.
 4. ex_stage: EX/MEM captures a bubble when replay_go (add to the `div_stall || redirect` branch; the `stall`
    branch above it still wins when dmem_stall), and div_op is gated with ~lu_q so a DIV/REM consumer of a
    load does not start the divider on stale operands. The bubble sequence downstream is identical to today
    (L in MEM, bubble, C), so the load-use cost stays 1 cycle and RVFI order / retirement is unchanged.
 5. core.sv: wire lu1_q/lu2_q/replay_go from hazard_unit to id_stage and ex_stage; forward_unit unchanged.

Corner cases checked on paper: redirect while lu_q (impossible, MEM holds a non-late_res branch, and lu_q is
cleared on redirect anyway); lu_q with dmem stall (hold both lu_q and ID/EX, replay on the first ready cycle);
C is a branch/store/MUL/DIV (operands recaptured before it executes, bubble hides the stale EX/MEM capture);
P1/P2 hits for the instruction behind C are ignored while it is stalled; dependent-load chains (L1 -> L2 -> use)
re-detect at ID against ID/EX.rd of the replaying instruction on the next consume.

Expected effect: timed critical path moves from head compare -> stall_id -> accept -> pc to flop -> LUT -> pc
(stall) with the compare ending at lu*_q D pins; remaining limiters (BHT read mux -> pred_raw -> next_pc, head ->
regfile read -> bypass -> ID/EX, ALU -> ex_res) set the new wall, so budget ~half of the stall-cone slack.

title: Carry-select fetch-side predicted-target adder with flop-only pc_hi +/-1 candidates
motivation:
Control-flow redirects are only ~63k of ~3.6M cycles (49.4k BHT mispredicts + 13.8k returns, 2
bubbles each), so a pure direction/target-accuracy change (RAS, bigger BHT, gshare) is capped at
~1-2% of cycles and was measured neutral or negative in r5s2/r10s2. The predictor's remaining
lever is its timing: decode-in-fetch computes pred_target = pc[31:2] + imm_sel[31:2] with a full
30-bit carry chain behind the late imem_data -> is_jal ? imm_j : imm_b mux, and that sum then
feeds the next_pc 2:1 mux, the redirect mux and the pc D pins, in two copies (imem_data and the
I-cache dout copy added in r11s2).

~1-2% of cycles and was measured neutral or negative in r5s2/r10s2. The predictor's remaining

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace both 30-bit pred_target adders with an exact carry-select form. The sign-extended upper
bits of a B/J immediate are all-0 or all-1, so the upper part of the target is one of
pc_hi, pc_hi+1, pc_hi-1, and all three candidates come from the pc flops alone (no imem_data in
front). Only a short low-part add (B: pc[12:2]+imm[12:2], 11 bits; J: pc[20:2]+imm[20:2], 19
bits, computed in parallel and chosen by is_jal) sits behind imem_data; its carry-out and the
immediate sign pick the upper candidate with one LUT level. The result is bit-exact for every
32-bit pc (formal explores pcs above 1 MB), so EX's direction-only validation is unchanged.
Cycles are identical by construction; the expected win is Fmax on the imem_data -> pred_target ->
next_pc -> pc/queue cone.

title: Stall network re-timing: per-source load-use compares selected by v0 at the last LUT, ID/EX hold split off stall_id (bit-identical cycles)
motivation:
The champion's recorded critical path (r11s2, 15.876 ns, 11 cells) is the stall cone
lfsr_20 = imem_data[20] / v0 -> `head = v0 ? e0 : fresh` -> head_rs1/2 -> hazard_unit
load-use compare against ID/EX.rd -> stall_id -> accept_f -> pc CE / I-cache rd_en /
ahead_ok / queue write enables. stall_id (dmem_stall | load_use | div_stall) is a very
high fan-out net (CE of ~230 ID/EX flops + queue + fetch accept), and its only late
input is the load-use term, which today pays an extra LUT level for the head mux in front
of the 5-bit compares (mux -> eq2/eq2/eq1 -> and3 -> or2 -> or with dmem/div -> accept).
Prior single attempts at this cone lost for reasons that this change avoids: r12s0 bundled
a bit-identical hold split with a *throughput-changing* conservative `accept = imem_ready &
~v1` (the 2-entry queue is full during every dmem/load-use stall, so it forfeited fetch
slots) and r12s1 replaced load-use by a replay with new select/enable terms on the
mem_res leg. This hypothesis does neither: no fetch-throughput change, no new term on the
mem_res -> ID/EX legs, no new bypass source; it only re-associates the existing boolean
function so the late term enters at the last LUT level.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep stall_id's logical function exactly as today, but restructure it in three
cycle-neutral ways, so the netlist behaves bit-identically (same cycle count, same RVFI
trace, formal/cosim unchanged).

(1) Parallel per-source load-use compare (hazard_unit.sv + if_stage.sv/core.sv wiring).
if_stage additionally exports the raw rs1/rs2 fields of the two possible head sources:
e0.instr[19:15], e0.instr[24:20] (queue flop) and imem_data[19:15], imem_data[24:20]
(fresh), plus the flop v0. hazard_unit computes
  lu_e0    = late_res & (id_ex_rd == e0_rs1    | id_ex_rd == e0_rs2)
  lu_fresh = late_res & (id_ex_rd == fresh_rs1 | id_ex_rd == fresh_rs2)
  load_use_hazard = v0 ? lu_e0 : lu_fresh
This is exactly the current `compare(head)` because head = v0 ? e0 : fresh, but the 3:1
head-mux LUT level that sits in front of every compare bit (and whose v0 select fans out
to 10 compare bits + the regfile read address bits) disappears from the stall cone; both
compares start straight at flops (the LFSR flop in the timed wrapper, the e0 flop), and v0
only enters in the last LUT together with the pre-ORed early term. head_rs1/head_rs2
(regfile read address, forward_unit) keep the existing head mux; nothing else changes.

(2) Early-term pre-merge: define hold_early = dmem_stall | div_stall (both are
flop-derived: dmem_ready from the stall generator flop & ex_mem mem-op flops, div_stall
from div_op/done flops) and write stall_id = hold_early | (v0 ? lu_e0 : lu_fresh), so the
late terms {v0, lu_e0, lu_fresh, hold_early} fit one LUT4 and accept
(= imem_ready & ~(v1 & stall_id)) / fill_acc / accept_f cost one more LUT, not two.
flush_id = (load_use | redirect) & ~dmem_stall reuses the same load_use net.

(3) ID/EX hold split. id_stage's ID/EX capture currently uses `stall` (= stall_id) as the
hold enable: `if (reset||flush) reg_q <= 0; else if (!stall) capture`. Because flush_id =
(load_use | redirect) & ~dmem_stall already has priority and a load-use hazard without
dmem_stall always asserts flush_id, the hold only needs hold_idex = dmem_stall | div_stall
(flop-derived, early). Add a `hold` input to id_stage driven by hold_early; ID/EX CE (~230
pins) leaves the load-use cone, which takes the biggest fan-out off stall_id and leaves it
driving only the fetch queue (v0/v1/e0/e1 next-state), the accept/fill/pc-CE/ahead_ok/
I-cache rd_en terms. Equivalence: load_use=1 & dmem_stall=1 -> flush_id=0, hold=1 (same
as before); load_use=1 & dmem_stall=0 -> flush_id=1 (same as before, flush has priority);
div_stall -> hold in both; redirect -> flush in both.

No change to the I-cache, BHT, predictor, bypass network, mem_stage, ex_stage, divider or
regfile. Cycle count must remain 3.57-3.59M (identical by construction); any cycle delta is
a bug. The expected gain is purely Fmax of the stall cone (one LUT level of ~5 on the
recorded top path, plus fan-out relief on stall_id), sized at ~+4-5% because the second

title: True IF/ID register on the fetch queue: ID reads flop e0 only, head mux and v0 select leave the stall/regfile/bypass cone
motivation:
The champion's recorded worst path (seed 0, arrival 15.876 ns, slack -5.58) is
lfsr_20 -> cpu/u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id -> u_if/pc_20 (11 cells): the imem_data word
goes through the `head = v0 ? e0 : fresh` mux, the head rs1/rs2 fields feed the
load-use compare, stall_id then feeds `accept` -> pc CE / I-cache rd_en / ahead_ok /
queue CEs. The same head bits also feed the 32:1 regfile read mux and the P1/P2
bypass compares. Tail-only trims of this cone lost (r12s0 conservative accept -7.66%,
r12s1 registered replay -5.84%) because the head mux and its v0 fan-out stayed at
the front, and r12s0's own path moved to the dmem -> mem_res -> alu_b leg at the same
~15.9 ns, i.e. the wall is flat and the head mux is the one shared front end still
in place. r8s1 (+6.98% on the r7s0 tree, 248.57 vs 232.36, 2 of 3 seeds at 102.9+)
proved the structural fix (ID always reads a flop entry; the extra redirect bubble
costs far less than the level it removes) but lost the ranking only because r8s0
merged first. It has never been re-applied, and the queue/pc cone it shortens is
now the champion's top endpoint (r11s2), which is not what r8s1 faced.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make e0 a true IF/ID register. The queue is already a 2-entry FIFO (e0 = oldest,
e1 = skid, v1 implies v0), so the change is small and local to if_stage:
  * head = e0 always; head_present = v0; emit = v0 & ~(flush | redirect).
  * the fresh word (and the I-cache filler word via fresh_q) is ALWAYS stored:
    store = accept (no `v0 | stall_id` bypass qualification), store_f = accept_f.
    The existing e0/e1/v0/v1 update equations (pop = v0 & ~stall_id; e0 <= e1 on
    pop with v1; fresh into e0 when the queue is empty after the pop; fresh into e1
    when occupied) are unchanged and already correct; accept keeps the same
    `imem_ready & ~(v1 & stall_id)` form so sustained throughput stays 1 word/cycle
    (a fresh word is stored into e0 on the same edge e0 is popped).
  * head_rs1 / head_rs2 / head.pc / head.instr / head.pred come straight from the e0
    flops. imem_data (an LFSR flop in the timed netlist, a BSRAM/bus word in a real
    system) now feeds only the decode-in-fetch predictor (pred_raw / pred_target ->
    next_pc -> pc D) and the e0/e1 D pins; it is no longer in front of the regfile
    read mux, forward compares, load-use compare or stall_id.
  * export small replica flops of e0.instr[19:15] / [24:20] (loaded on the same
    conditions as e0) so the regfile read halves, forward_unit and hazard_unit each
    see a low-fan-out copy (mark them syn_keep-style or compute them from the
    identical D input so the mapper does not merge them; drop the replicas if timing
    shows no benefit).
Cost: a taken-branch/JALR redirect now refills e0 one cycle later (+1 bubble per
redirect, redirects ~2-3% of instructions, so ~2% cycles, same cost r8s1 paid and
still came out ahead); dmem / load-use / div stalls and imem stalls behave as today
because e0 is refilled in the pop cycle and the I-cache filler still writes only
the queue flops. Do NOT touch the I-cache read address (pc+4, CE = accept_f), the
agree-BHT, the registered EX redirect, the 30-bit `+` target adders, or the
mem_res / DSP / dmem-address cones; keep `redirect` out of the pc-CE cone.
Expected: the head-mux level and v0 select removed from the stall -> accept -> pc CE
cone and from the head_rs -> read mux -> bypass -> ID/EX cone, worth roughly +7%
Fmax on the champion's top path family, minus ~2% cycles. Record Fmax and cycles
separately in the implementation notes. Formal (rvfi order/liveness) is unaffected
because retirement order is set at EX/MEM/WB; the only new behaviour is the extra
fetch-to-ID cycle.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r13s1 (regression, -2.75%): Re-applying r8s1's true IF/ID register on the r11s2 champion tree (ID reads only the e0 flops with valid = v0, `head = v0 ? e0 : fresh` deleted, `store_f = accept_f` so every word goes through the queue flops, one extra bubble per redirect; the minimal form with no rs-field replicas and no pre-decoded ctrl/imm) reached 277.95 vs 285.82 against a ~+5% prediction, so the +6.98% r8s1 measured on the r7s0 tree did not transfer: that gain came from taking the head mux and `v0` select out of the then-limiting head_rs -> 32:1 read mux -> bypass -> ID/EX cone, but on the champion the wall had already moved to the ~15.9 ns dmem BSRAM -> `mem_res` -> ID/EX `alu_b` leg (r12s0), which this edit does not touch, so the ~2% redirect-bubble cycle cost is paid with nothing shortening the real endpoint (no Fmax/cycle split or critical path was recorded, so this is inferred); the result sits just above the 264-269 band that cycle-neutral perturbations (r12s0/s1/s2, r13s0) fell into, so drop front-end head/stall-cone trims as a lever and spend the next attempt on the `mem_res` -> ID/EX `alu_b` / dmem-address cone, and do not re-apply a gain measured on an older tree without first re-reading the current worst path.

title: Branch-target word table: fill the imem-stall slot at every predicted-taken target from a BSRAM read addressed by the branch pc
motivation:
I ran the CoreMark ELF through test/cosim/reference.py (2,937,037 retired instrs, champion r11s2 = 3,572,308 cycles)
and modeled where the 635k non-retiring cycles go: load-use ~205k (204,777 pairs), dmem stalls ~193k
(689k memops x 0.22/0.78), redirects ~126k (49.4k BHT mispredicts of 532k branches with the exact 128-entry
agree BHT + 13.8k JALR, x2 bubbles), MUL consumers ~45k, and the residue (~65k) is imem stall slots the filler
cache still cannot cover. Predictor tweaks on the direction side are exhausted (perfect prediction would be
3.5% of cycles; RAS/hash/BTIB all lost to Fmax). The residue is NOT capacity: a trace-driven model of the
direct-mapped filler shows 2048 -> 4096 words only moves sequential misses 0.55% -> 0.08% of fetches
(~0.1% of cycles), so a bigger cache is worthless. What the filler structurally cannot cover is the fetch
at a predicted-taken target (and the first fetch after any redirect): ahead_ok is cleared on a taken accept
because the BSRAM address is pc+4, not the late pred_target. Non-sequential fetches are 12.2% of all
instructions (358k); a stall (22%) there starves ID outright because the queue was just cut off at the branch:
~0.28 x 358k = ~100k cycles (~2.8% of cycles) of which the part not hidden by a buffered entry is the target.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a branch-target word table (rtl/icache.sv gets a second small port/array, or a new rtl/tgt_table.sv):
512 entries indexed by the BRANCH's pc[10:2], each {valid, branch tag pc[19:11], target word}. Because B-type
and JAL targets are static (pc + imm), the word at the target of a given branch pc never changes, so the
entry is exact whenever the branch tag matches.
- Read: BSRAM address = pc[10:2] straight from the pc flop (same flop-only rule as the champion's pc+4
  read, CE = accept_f). The registered dout therefore holds the target word of the branch at P during the
  cycle pc = T. A flop `tw_sel` = (accept_f & predicted-taken at P) & ~redirect/reset marks that the table,
  not the sequential cache, belongs to the current pc; 9 flops keep P's tag bits for the compare.
- Use: fill_hit becomes ~imem_ready & ((ahead_ok & ic_valid & tag_ok) | (tw_sel & tw_valid & tw_tag == p_tag)).
  The word enters ONLY the e0/e1 D inputs through the existing fresh_q mux (one extra flop-selected 2:1 on the
  data leg); head = v0 ? e0 : fresh and fresh.instr = imem_data are untouched.
- Only NON-control target words are stored (opcode not B-type/JAL, checked at write time), so the filler's next
  pc is plain pc+4 and no third decode-in-fetch cone / adder is needed: next_pc = imem_ready ? old :
  ((~tw_sel & pred_raw_c) ? pred_target_c : pc4), tw_sel being a flop (the duplicated cone on the sequential
  cache dout stays as is). The queue entry's pred bit is 0 for table words.
- Write: from registered ID/EX flops only (never raw imem_data), like the champion's cache: a flop pair
  {last_tk_v, last_tk_pc} is set when a valid pred_taken instruction sits in ID/EX; the next valid, un-redirected
  ID/EX instruction (the target word, wr_valid & ~redirect) writes table[last_tk_pc[10:2]] <= {1, tag, wr_instr}
  if wr_instr is non-control. Wrong-path writes are harmless: the entry is keyed by the branch pc and the
  word is only used when the next accepted pc really is a predicted-taken target; a stale/aliased entry is
  rejected by the 9-bit tag compare and, since code is static, a matching entry is correct.
Budget: ~512 x 42 bits = ~2 BSRAM blocks (9 of 46 used today), ~25 LUTs, ~20 FFs. Expected cycles: -1.5% to
-2.5% (the 12.2% non-sequential fetches x 22% stall x queue-empty share, minus control-word targets and
cold/aliased misses). Expected Fmax risk: one extra OR leg in fill_hit -> fill_acc -> accept_f (the 9-bit compare is
flop vs BSRAM dout, same shape as the existing 7-bit one). If `make timing` shows that cone getting longer,
fall back to storing a 1-bit "exact" flag in the entry at write time (the writer already knows the branch
pc and index, and the code is static) and drop the in-cycle tag compare in favor of that single bit AND
tw_sel, accepting a few aliased misses. Record Fmax and cycles separately; this is a cycle-only change by design.

Add tw_sel and prev-pc-tag flops, the table-hit term in fill_hit, the filler data mux (table dout vs sequential cache dout) on the fresh_q data leg only, last_tk_v/last_tk_pc capture from ID/EX (wr_valid & pred_taken input), and the (~tw_sel & pred_raw_c) gate in the filler next_pc; leave head mux, imem_data path, redirect priority and BHT untouched.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r13s2 (regression, -13.41%): A 512-entry branch-target word table (second BSRAM read at the branch's `pc[10:2]`, flop `tw_sel` + 9-bit `tw_tag == p_tag` compare OR'd into `fill_hit`, `tw_sel ? tw_data : ic_data` on `fresh_q.instr`, `pred_c_g = ~tw_sel & pred_raw_c` on `next_pc`/`ahead_ok`, ID/EX-fed training flops) reached 247.48 vs r11s2's 285.82 against a ~2% cycle ceiling, and since the change is cycle-neutral-or-better by construction the ~13% loss must be Fmax (no Fmax/cycle split or critical path was recorded, so the mechanism is inferred) from hanging a BSRAM-dout compare and extra legs on the `fill_hit -> fill_acc -> accept_f` (pc CE / `rd_en` / `ahead_ok`) cone that r11s2 won by keeping flop-only, and it shipped the in-cycle tag compare that its own notes said to replace with a write-time `exact` bit; the fetch-accept cone has no slack for a gain bounded at ~2% of cycles, so any further imem-stall coverage must add zero logic levels there (flop-only select, no compare) or not be attempted.

title: Regfile write from MEM/WB flops (fanout-1 mem_res) with a flop-sourced P3 bypass leg in ID
motivation:
The last five rounds of cycle-neutral timing edits (r12s0/s1/s2, r13s0/s1) all landed at 264-278 MHz-equivalent
fitness with the worst endpoint at dmem BSRAM -> u_mem (load extract, mem_to_reg mux) -> u_id (ID/EX
rs1_val / rs2_val / alu_b D), ~15.9 ns. Every one of those edits trimmed select/stall logic and none touched the
net that is actually on that path: `mem_res`. Since r8s0 the regfile is written from MEM with w_data = mem_res, so
each of the 32 mem_res bits drives 31 regfile D pins (one per x1..x31 flop, spread across the whole regfile
area) PLUS the three ID/EX bypass legs. That is a ~34-pin net hanging directly off the BSRAM output after the
extract LUTs, which costs routing delay on the one net the placer cannot shorten by moving the regfile near the
bypass muxes. r8s0's gain came from deleting compare/mux levels on the head_rs -> read mux cone, not from the
write-port timing; the stage-early write added this fanout as a stated caveat ("cheap only while mem_res fan-out to
the 31x32 D pins stays shallower than the existing alu_b leg"). The wall is now exactly that leg.
Measured on the current tree with `make timing TARGET=bench` (placement option 0, 94.5 MHz): the top five endpoints
are a flat wall at 15.87-15.88 ns in three families: (a) imem lfsr -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id -> pc D (fetch/stall
cone), (b) dmem BSRAM -> u_mem -> u_id alu_b / rs2_val (the mem_res net, paths 2-3), (c) ID/EX rs1_val -> u_alu ->
EX/MEM.alu_result (paths 4-5). This proposal attacks family (b) only, so the honest expectation is that it removes
one of three co-limiting families and the gain is capped at the gap to (a)/(c), which is ~0 in this report; it is
proposed because it is the only family-(b) edit that adds no select/enable term to the late mem_res legs
(the failure mode of r12s1, r11s0, r13s0) and is cycle-neutral by construction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the architectural regfile write back to WB, but source it from flops so the mem_res net no longer reaches
the regfile, and replace the lost write-first coverage with a single flop-data P3 bypass leg in ID:
(1) mem_stage: add one flop `wb_data` to MEM/WB (D = mem_res, the existing mux output; load/extract logic
    unchanged, it already feeds reg_q.read_data) - or reuse wb_stage's w_data mux from the existing
    read_data/alu_result flops. The regfile write port becomes
      w_en   = mem_wb_w.valid & mem_wb_w.ctrl.reg_write   (valid is already cleared on hold_wb, so a
                                                            dmem-stalled op writes exactly once)
      w_addr = mem_wb_w.rd
      w_data = flop-sourced WB value (no logic, fanout 31 only on flop outputs).
    mem_res then fans out only to the 3 ID/EX bypass legs + 1 MEM/WB flop (was 3 + 31).
(2) forward_unit: add p3_hit_rs1/p3_hit_rs2 = wb_res_en && (wb_rd == head_rs{1,2}) where wb_res_en is the
    registered MEM/WB valid&reg_write bit. Same style as p1/p2 (raw hits, priority P1 > P2 > P3 > regfile).
(3) id_stage: apply P3 on the EARLY side only: rf_eff = p3 ? wb_data : rs_data (flop data, so it is parallel to the
    read mux and sits behind head_rs/p3 compare but not behind mem_res/ex_res), then keep the final levels
    unchanged: rs1_val <= p1 ? ex_res : p2 ? mem_res : rf_eff; alu_b AND-OR gets b_sel_rf = ~alu_src & ~p1 & ~p2
    with the rf leg replaced by rf_eff (b_sel_p3 folded into rf_eff, no new term on the late legs).
Cycle count is bit-identical to the champion (same bypass coverage, same hazard unit, same stall behaviour);
RVFI order/retirement is untouched because RVFI already reads MEM/WB. Formal: the regfile still observes
exactly one write per retired instruction, and the P3 bypass restores the old WB-write architectural view
(instruction in WB at cycle t is visible to ID at cycle t), so riscv-formal reg/pc_fwd checks see the same values.
Risk/expected effect: re-adds one flop-data mux level on the head_rs -> read mux -> bypass cone (r8s0 removed
three such levels; this is the cheapest of them, a 2:1 on early data) in exchange for cutting 31 D-pin loads
off the BSRAM -> extract -> mem_res net that is the current wall. Fail-safe: if timing shows the rf cone is

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes: regfile written from MEM/WB flops + early P3 leg

## What changed (matches the hypothesis plan)

- `core.sv`: the regfile write port is back on the WB stage and is flop-sourced:
  `wb_res_en = mem_wb_w.valid && mem_wb_w.ctrl.reg_write`,
  `rf_w_en = wb_res_en`, `rf_w_addr = mem_wb_w.rd`, `rf_w_data = wb_w_data`
  (the existing `wb_stage` mux of `read_data` / `alu_result`). `mem_res` no longer
  feeds the 31x32 regfile D pins; it now only feeds the three ID/EX bypass legs
  (rs1_val, rs2_val, alu_b) and the MEM/WB capture. New wires `p3_hit_rs1/2`,
  `wb_res_en`; `wb_w_data` is also passed to `id_stage` as `wb_res`.
- `forward_unit.sv`: new inputs `wb_rd`, `wb_res_en`; new outputs
  `p3_hit_rs1 / p3_hit_rs2 = wb_res_en && (wb_rd == rs)`. All flop-sourced
  (plus the existing head_rs compare inputs). P1 and P2 are unchanged.
- `id_stage.sv`: new inputs `wb_res`, `p3_hit_rs1/2`. The P3 select is merged
  with the regfile read first, on the early side:
  `rf1 = p3_hit_rs1 ? wb_res : rs1_data` (same for rf2). Then
  `rs1_val = p1 ? ex_res : p2 ? mem_res : rf1` (same for rs2_val) and the alu_b
  one-hot AND-OR keeps its four legs with the regfile leg replaced by `rf2`
  (`b_sel_rf` unchanged: p3 is already folded into rf2). The late `ex_res` /
  `mem_res` legs therefore see the same mux depth as before.
- `reg_file.sv`: no functional change (plain combinational read, no write-first),
  header comment updated. `wb_stage.sv` / `mem_stage.sv`: comment updates only.

## Correctness argument

- Write timing: the instruction in WB in cycle t writes at the end of t. The
  instruction in ID in cycle t reads the old regfile value, which is corrected by
  P3 (priority P1 > P2 > P3 > regfile, i.e. youngest writer wins).
- `mem_wb_w.valid` gates the write and the P3 hit. A dmem-held MEM/WB
  (`hold_mem_wb`) has `valid = 0` with data retained: its write already happened
  in the previous cycle, so there is neither a second write nor a repeat P3 hit.
  Bubbles / squashed slots have `valid = 0` (and `ctrl = '0`) as well.
- `ctrl.reg_write` in MEM/WB already has `rd != 0` folded in (id_stage) and the
  EX/MEM misalign trap clears (ex_stage `ctrl_with_trap`, mem_stage
  `ctrl_with_trap`), so x0 is never written / forwarded and trapped
  instructions do not write or forward.
- Every producer is visible to a consumer at exactly one of: EX (P1), MEM (P2),
  WB (P3) or the regfile, so there is no gap, including across dmem / divide
  stalls (the capture only happens when ID is not stalled and the selects are
  re-evaluated every cycle).
- RVFI is unchanged (driven from the MEM/WB register as before; the bypass
  produces the same values as the previous regfile read).
- Pipeline timing, stalls, hazards, load-use and cycle counts are unchanged.

## Deviations

None. The write-first-in-regfile fallback mentioned in the hypothesis was NOT
used (see timing note below).

## Concerns

- New early-side logic: two 5-bit equality compares (`wb_rd == head_rs1/2`) and one
  2:1 mux per operand (x2 for rs1/rs2, 32 bits each) between the regfile 32:1
  read mux and the late bypass legs. The head_rs -> read mux -> P3 mux ->
  ID/EX cone is one LUT level deeper than before; the hypothesis predicts this is
  paid for by the removal of the ~31-load fanout from the BSRAM-dout `mem_res`
  net. If `make timing` shows this early cone as the new worst path, the
  fallback is a write-first read inside the regfile.

## Local verification

- `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP`: clean.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`
  (auto-selects wrapper_si.sv / checks_si.cfg for `nret: 1`): 53 passed, 0 failed.
  (Note: `make formal TARGET=bench` passes `formal/checks.cfg` explicitly, which
  is the nret=2 config, and fails on missing `_1` ports; that is a Makefile/config
  mismatch for this nret=1 core, not an RTL problem.)
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` (plain `make cosim` builds with the default
  `-DNRET=2` and fails to compile against this nret=1 core's missing `_1` ports):
  passed, 2 ELFs (selftest + CoreMark CRCs under stalls).
- `make timing TARGET=bench` (Gowin, place_option 0 only was printed): Fmax
  97.576 MHz, 12 logic levels, LUT4 logic 4455, regs 2048, BSRAM 9, DSP 2. The
  five worst paths (15.53-15.54 ns) are all flop-to-flop inside EX/ID/IF:
  `u_id/reg_q.rs2_val -> u_ex/reg_q.pc_next` (branch compare), `rs1_val ->
  alu_result` / `alu_b`, and `u_ic BSRAM -> u_if/pc`. The dmem BSRAM dout ->
  u_mem -> u_id (P2 bypass) family that was the worst endpoint in earlier
  runs, and the new P3 / regfile-read cone, are not among them, so the
  hypothesis' target path is no longer the wall. core.yaml's recorded
  `current` Fmax is 102.102 MHz (median of 3 placement options); this single
  option run is 97.6 MHz, so whether the net median improves needs the
  evaluator's 3-option run. I did not attempt the write-first fallback because the
  P3 cone is not on the reported worst paths.

title: Local-history branch predictor trained off the fetch cone: per-branch history + pattern table write a precomputed 1-bit predict flop array
motivation:
Measured on the champion (full RVFI trace of the timed CoreMark window, 2.92M instrs / 3.57M cycles, CPI 1.22).
An offline model of the current 128-entry agree-BHT reproduces the hardware exactly: 529,588 branches,
49,011 mispredicts (every one is gap=3 at retire, i.e. 2.40 lost cycles) = 117.7k cycles = 3.3% of the window.
JALR adds 13.7k redirects = 0.9%, load-use is 6.2% (not a predictor problem).
Where the mispredicts come from: global history does not help at all (gshare 2..8 bits is 40.5k-58k, never better than the plain 39.5k
of a 256+ entry pc-indexed table); doubling the table to 256 entries only removes aliasing (49.0k -> 39.6k). The
remaining ~39.6k are dominated by loop exits of short FIXED-trip-count loops (CRC bit loops of 8,
trip-9 matrix/list loops; 14.6k backward-not-taken mispredicts, top PCs 0x1a44/0x191c each miss exactly every 8th execution)
and forward branches inside them that follow a per-branch periodic pattern. A per-branch (local) history of
8 bits captures exactly that (ideal 8-bit local history: 19.9k mispredicts).
Past predictor slots lost on Fmax, not on idea: r10s2 put an XOR in front of the BHT read mux, r8s2/r9s2/r13s2 hung compares and
extra sources on imem_data / accept / fill_hit. The fetch-side cone is the reason: it must stay byte-for-byte what r11s2 has.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the fetch cone unchanged: pred_raw still uses ONE bit read from a flop array indexed by pc[8:2] (today that bit is
bht[pc[8:2]][1] = ctr_hi, 128:1 mux, dir = ctr_hi ? bias : ~bias). The array becomes `ap[128]` ("agree-predict" bit)
that is not a counter MSB but a precomputed prediction for the NEXT dynamic instance of that branch. All the new logic is on the
training side, driven by the already-registered EX/MEM update port (bht_upd_en/idx/taken/bwd), 2-3 cycles after resolution:
  U0 (cycle the branch is in EX/MEM): read local history h = LH[idx] (128 x 8-bit, LUT-RAM or flops, async read is fine, update side only);
      read pattern counter c = PT[{pc[3:2], h}] (256 x 4... 1024 x 2-bit, or BSRAM with registered address).
  U1: write PT[{pc[3:2],h}] = c +/-1 (agree encoding, init 2'b10 so a cold pattern falls back to the BTFN bias exactly like today);
      write LH[idx] = {h[6:0], outcome}; with h' = {h[6:0], outcome} read PT[{pc[3:2],h'}] and write
      ap[idx] <= PT[...][1]  (agree encoding; reset value 1 = static BTFN like the current reset 2'b10).
Hardware numbers from the trace-driven model with the real 4-cycle fetch->update visibility lag
(pending updates applied only when the branch executed >= 4 cycles earlier), H=128 entries, 8-bit history, 2 pc bits in the pattern index:
28.7k mispredicts vs 49.0k baseline (lag 0: 27.3k); H=256 entries: 26.6k (but a 256:1 read mux, so prefer 128);
10-bit history + 4 pc bits H=256: 21.8k. Saving ~20-27k mispredicts x 2.4 cycles = 49k-65k cycles = 1.4-1.8% of the window
(also drops the 128x2 reset BHT counters; the remaining reset state is 128 ap flops).
No wide compares, no new term in accept / head_present / pc CE, no change to imem_data fanout, no new source in front of
the fetch queue; the predictor tables only see registered EX/MEM flops. If Gowin maps LH/PT to SSRAM/BSRAM make sure
the formal checks still pass (the tables are pure control state; pc_fwd / liveness do not depend on their contents) and keep
an ifdef-free implementation. Recommended implementation order: (1) land the ap[] + update pipeline with a plain counter
update and verify the cycle count is unchanged, (2) enable the local-history path and compare cycles and `make timing` Fmax separately.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r14s2 (regression, -1.26%): Moving conditional-branch prediction to a train-only local-history pipeline (fetch cone kept to one `ap[pc[8:2]]` flop read in place of the BHT counter MSB; 128x9-bit `lh` plus 1024-entry `pt_a`/`pt_b` pattern tables with async reads, three A/B/C stages off the registered EX/MEM update port with same-index/same-address forwarding, 1 pc bit in the pattern index, history recording the agree bit) reached 282.22 vs r11s2's 285.82, so even a predictor that leaves the fetch cone untouched does not convert a cycle-only gain into fitness: the entire conditional-mispredict pool is only ~3.3% of the timed window (49k x 2.4 cycles) and local history was modeled to recover just ~1.4-1.8% of it, below both the ~4.6% merge margin and the 264-289 spread that cycle-neutral netlist perturbations of r11s2 produce (r12s0/s1/s2, r13s0); no Fmax/cycle split was recorded, so whether the extra ~4.2k bits of table state cost Fmax or the cycles did not drop as modeled is unknown, but treat conditional-branch prediction as exhausted (a perfect predictor is worth <3.3%) and record cycles and Fmax separately before spending another predictor slot.

title: One-hot pre-decoded EX result select: flat AND-OR ex_res over parallel dedicated units, no op decode or nested jump/div/mul muxes behind the ALU
motivation:
The champion (r11s2, 285.82) sits on a flat ~15.9 ns wall of three near-equal endpoint families:
(a) the fetch/stall cone, (b) dmem BSRAM -> load extract -> mem_res -> ID/EX bypass legs, and
(c) ID/EX rs1_val -> ALU -> ex_res -> EX/MEM.alu_result (and the P1 bypass into ID/EX). Cycle-neutral
edits that touch only one family (r12s0/s1/s2, r13s0, r14s0) all landed in the 264-289 band, so a
single-family fix is capped at the gap to its neighbours. Family (c) is the only one whose logic is
still structurally deep and fully under RTL control: ex_res is built as a 5-bit `case (op)` decode ->
~11-way mux inside alu.sv, then a nested `is_jump|is_auipc ? (is_jump ? pc+4 : branch_target) :
(div_op ? div_result : alu_out)` in ex_stage, then the `mul_lo ? p_lo : mul_hi ? p_hi : ex_res` merge.
That is a 5-bit decode plus roughly five mux levels behind the adder / shifter / comparator outputs, with
every decoded select driving a fanout-32 net. r10s0 tried a flat one-hot result and lost (-5.97%), but it
bundled that with merging the adder/compare/shifter into shared hardware (b ^ sub in front of the carry
chain, carry-out slt, bit-reversing shifter) and its own notes say the flat select should be tested as its
own change while keeping the dedicated parallel units. This hypothesis is exactly that isolated change.
Re-measured on the current tree with `make timing TARGET=bench` (place_option 0, 94.5 MHz): paths 4-5 are
ID/EX rs1_val -> u_alu -> EX/MEM alu_result at 15.87 ns / 9 cells, tied with the fetch cone (path 1, 11 cells)
and the dmem -> u_mem -> u_id alu_b/rs2_val cone (paths 2-3, 7-8 cells), so family (c) is a co-limiter, not a
slack path, and it is the one with the most removable mux levels.

chain, carry-out slt, bit-reversing shifter) and its own notes say the flat select should be tested as its
own change while keeping the dedicated parallel units. This hypothesis is exactly that isolated change.
Re-measured on the current tree with `make timing TARGET=bench` (place_option 0, 94.5 MHz): paths 4-5 are
ID/EX rs1_val -> u_alu -> EX/MEM alu_result at 15.87 ns / 9 cells, tied with the fetch cone (path 1, 11 cells)
and the dmem -> u_mem -> u_id alu_b/rs2_val cone (paths 2-3, 7-8 cells), so family (c) is a co-limiter, not a
slack path, and it is the one with the most removable mux levels.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move all result-select decoding out of EX into the decoder, as one-hot ctrl flops captured in ID/EX, and
make ex_res one flat AND-OR over the existing, unchanged parallel units:
  legs: r_add (a+b), r_sub (a-b), r_and, r_or, r_xor, r_slt, r_sltu, r_sll, r_srl, r_sra, r_b (LUI = alu_b),
        r_pc4 (JAL/JALR return address), r_auipc (pc+imm from the existing PC adder), r_div (divider result).

    exactly one is set for any ALU / jump / auipc / lui / div op, none for loads, stores, branches,

collapse to 7 first-level LUTs and 2 OR levels. The same ex_res net feeds both EX/MEM.alu_result and the P1
bypass into the three ID/EX capture legs, so the shortening applies to both consumers of family (c) at once.

placement re-rolled to the 264-269 band with no endpoint change, the result is a null — judged on the
multi-seed median, not one run.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-001-r15s0 (regression, -2.71%): Testing the flat one-hot EX result select as its own change, as r10s0's notes asked (14 pre-decoded `sel` flops in ID/EX, `ex_res` as one AND-OR over the unchanged parallel adder/subtractor/slt/sltu/shifters/logic/pc4/auipc/div legs, `alu_result_d = ex_res | mul_lo&p_lo | mul_hi&p_hi`), reached 278.08 vs r11s2's 285.82 at cycles identical by construction, so r10s0's -5.97% was not just its adder/shifter merging, and removing the `case (op)` decode and the jump/div/mul mux nesting from behind the ALU does not move this wall: the result sits inside the 264-289 band that every cycle-neutral perturbation of r11s2 lands in (r12s0/s1/s2, r13s0, r14s0), and no post-change critical path was recorded, so inferred, but the +14 fanout-32 flops and the extra AND terms plausibly cost as many LUT levels and as much routing as the 5-6 mux levels they replace on a path already tied at ~15.9 ns with the fetch/stall and dmem `mem_res` -> ID/EX cones; drop EX result-select restructuring as a lever and do not retry it unless it is bundled with a change that also shortens the `mem_res` -> ID/EX or fetch cone, and judge any further cycle-neutral timing edit on a multi-seed median rather than one run.

title: Raw load-data capture in MEM/WB (BSRAM leaves the bypass loop) + e0-only accept cone
motivation:
Every recent champion-tree run ends on the same two endpoints. The median-seed
champion path is lfsr(imem_data) -> head_rs -> load-use compare -> stall_id ->
accept/pc CE (11 cells, 15.88 ns arrival). The other runs (r8s0, r9s0, r9s1,
r12s0, r12s1, r14s0) all end at dmem BSRAM -> u_mem (byte shift / sign extend /
mem_to_reg) -> u_id bypass -> ID/EX alu_b / rs1_val / rs2_val at 15.2-16.1 ns.
The ALU cone is a bit shorter (r8s1: alu_b -> alu_result, 14.8 ns). Single-cone
trims of either family (r12s0, r12s1, r13s0, r14s0) landed at 264-289, because
the other family holds the wall. Every LUT-level trim behind the BSRAM output
(r9s0 +1.8%, r11s0 -8.7%) is exhausted, since the BSRAM clock-to-out itself is the
big fixed term. This hypothesis changes the structure so that the BSRAM output
only feeds a flop. It also takes the fresh-word compare out of the accept cone.
Both families are cut in one change, which is what the r14s0 lesson asks for.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) Move load extraction from MEM to WB. mem_stage captures the RAW 32-bit
dmem_rdata word, plus the already-registered lane/width/sext controls, into
MEM/WB. No byte shift, sign extend or mem_to_reg mux sits behind the BSRAM
output any more, so the BSRAM -> ID/EX path disappears. BSRAM -> flop is only
clock-to-out plus setup. wb_stage does shift/extend from MEM/WB flops and
produces wb_w_data = mem_to_reg ? extract(raw) : alu_result. This is also the
RVFI rd_wdata, which is unchanged.
The extra bypass work then sits on a flop-sourced path, roughly flop -> 2
extract levels -> bypass AND-OR -> ID/EX, about 8-9 ns instead of ~10 ns plus
BSRAM tco.
(2) Regfile write port moves to WB (w_en = mem_wb.valid && ctrl.reg_write,
w_data = wb_w_data). ID gets a P3 bypass leg from wb_w_data.
forward_unit adds p3_hit_rs1/rs2 (rd compare against mem_wb.rd, with
reg_write && valid folded in; the existing rd != 0 folding makes x0 never hit).
The priority is P1 > P2 > P3 > regfile. The P2 leg (EX/MEM) can only be an ALU
or JAL result, because loads in MEM are never bypassed. Its mem_res is simply
EX/MEM.alu_result, a flop, so the mem_res cone from the BSRAM disappears.
hold_wb still clears valid only, so a stalled dmem cycle neither rewrites the
regfile nor hits P3.
(3) The load-use hazard becomes 2-cycle for loads. hazard_unit adds a second term:
mem_read in EX/MEM (a load now in MEM) with ex_mem.rd == head_rs1/rs2 also
stalls ID (stall_id and flush_id as for the existing term). A dist-1 consumer
takes 2 bubbles, a dist-2 consumer takes 1. mul keeps its single late_res bubble
(its product is in EX/MEM.alu_result, which is a P2 flop leg). The extra
cycles are budgeted at roughly 1-2% (gcc's default rocket tune already schedules
loads away from their consumers; loads are about 20% of instructions and the
extra penalty applies only to the dist-1 and dist-2 consumers).
(4) Take the fresh word out of the accept cone. When v1 = 1 the head is e0
(v1 implies v0), so stall_id equals a flop-only expression. Define
stall_e0 = dmem_stall | div_stall | late_res_hit(id_ex vs e0 rs1/rs2) | the new
dist-2 hit vs e0. Use it in `accept = imem_ready & ~(v1 & stall_e0)` and
`fill_acc`. This is exactly equivalent when v1 = 1, and the term is masked when
v1 = 0. The STA no longer sees the false path imem_data -> head mux -> compare ->
stall_id -> pc CE / I-cache rd_en / ahead_ok. The full stall_id (head mux
retained) still drives the ID/EX hold and pop of the queue.
Keep decoder, alu, divider, icache, BHT, DSP merge and dedicated maddr adder
as is. RVFI fields are untouched. Under ALTOPS nothing changes except the
stall/bypass plumbing, which the formal wrapper already exercises.
Expected: BSRAM family from ~15.9 ns to ~12-13 ns, the pc/stall family loses the
fresh-word compare, and the ALU cone (~14.8 ns) becomes the wall. The aim is
Fmax of 105-108 MHz in the median seed. Cycles are +1-3%. If the cost is too
high, drop part (3)'s dist-2 term by forwarding the raw MEM word through a
second compare-free path only for LW (no extract), but only after measuring.
Record Fmax and cycles separately in implementation_notes, and run `make
timing` to read the post-change worst endpoint before finalizing.

title: Prediction-steered recovery target: derive EX/MEM.pc_next from the carried pred_taken bit so the 32-bit branch compare leaves the redirect-target cone (RVFI next-pc split off and pruned)
motivation:
Measured facts from the log. Champion r11s2: 3,572,308 cycles, 102.1 MHz median (seeds 94.5/102.1/102.1).
The conditional-mispredict pool is ~3.3% of the window and JALR redirects ~0.9%, so any pure direction/target
predictor is cycle-capped at a few percent: r14s2's local-history predictor did deliver the cycles (3,508,601,
-1.8%) but lost 3% Fmax to placement noise and scored -1.26%. Direction/target prediction accuracy is therefore
exhausted as a lever (r5s2, r8s2, r9s2, r10s2, r13s2, r14s2). The remaining predictor-side lever is to USE the
prediction that is already carried into EX to shorten the recovery cone. Today EX computes
branch_cond (32-bit eq/lt/ltu carry chain) -> branch_taken -> misalign_branch -> misalign_fault -> a 4-way
select that builds the 32-bit EX/MEM.pc_next (the registered redirect target). r14s1's `make timing` shows exactly
this family among the flat ~15.5 ns top paths: u_id/reg_q.rs2_val -> u_ex/reg_q.pc_next_24 with 37 cells / 12 logic
levels. But the redirect target never needs the compare: IF already steered the next fetch, so when EX asks for a
redirect (redir = actual_dir ^ pred_taken, or JALR) the correct target is fully determined by flops:
pred_taken=1 (it was not taken) -> pc+4; pred_taken=0 (it was taken) -> pc+imm; JALR -> jalr_sum. The compare is
only needed for the 1-bit `redir` / `branch_taken` flops. The real next-pc (compare-dependent, also covers the
misalign-trap suppression) is needed only for RVFI pc_wdata, which the timed netlist prunes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the next-pc into two fields in ex_stage / ex_mem_t:
  * pc_next   (redirect target; the only one that reaches redirect_target -> if_stage pc mux):
      is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : (in.pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm)
    Selects are ID/EX flop bits (ctrl.is_jalr, pred_taken): no branch_cond, no branch_taken, no misalign_fault in
    this cone. Only the two existing flop-fed adders (pc+imm, pc+4) and jalr_sum feed a flat 3:1 mux. This value is
    only consumed when redir = 1; when redir = 0 it is a don't-care for fetch, so it is always safe.
    (JAL: always predicted taken unless imm[1] is set, in which case misalign_fault suppresses redir, so the
    "pred_taken ? pc+4" arm is never consumed for JAL.)
  * pc_next_r (architectural next pc for RVFI pc_wdata): exactly today's expression
      misalign_fault ? pc+4 : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_taken ? branch_target : pc+4,
    stored in a new ex_mem_t field and forwarded to mem_wb_t.pc_next. It feeds only io_rvfi_pc_wdata_0, so the
    Gowin netlist (memory-side outputs only) prunes it together with its compare-dependent select; formal and
    cosim still see the identical RVFI behaviour.
Also simplify the 1-bit consumers of the compare so they are as shallow as possible: misalign_branch =
is_branch & branch_cond & imm[1] (pc is word aligned, so branch_target[1:0] == imm[1:0] and imm[0] is 0; this drops
the pc+imm adder from the misalign cone), keeping redir_nxt = (is_jalr | (actual_dir ^ pred_taken)) & ~misalign_fault
as the only compare-fed redirect flop.
Nothing in fetch, the BHT, the queue, the I-cache filler, hazard, forwarding or the ID cone changes, so cycles are
identical by construction (redirect timing, penalty and squash behaviour are unchanged) and the BHT training port
(branch_taken / bwd flops) is untouched. The new logic is a net reduction (the old 4-way 32-bit select with the
compare-dependent selects disappears from the timed netlist; the RVFI copy is pruned).
Honest sizing: this removes one of the several near-equal ~15.5 ns families (compare -> pc_next), and the log says
single-family fixes are capped at the gap to the next family (r14s0, r6s0, r13s0), so the expected gain is small and
mainly a check that the flat wall is not simply this endpoint; it is deliberately a single separable change with no
cycle risk, so any result can be read as a pure Fmax signal.
